name: Late-onset Idiopathic Chronic Pancreatitis
aliases: Late-Onset Chronic Pancreatitis of Unknown Etiology

criteria.description: Evidence of chronic pancreatic inflammation on imaging or histology
No history of significant alcohol consumption or other known etiologies
Presence of pancreatic exocrine insufficiency demonstrated by malabsorption or fecal elastase testing
Recurrent or chronic epigastric abdominal pain consistent with pancreatitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of chronic pancreatic inflammation on imaging or histology AND absence of other known causes including alcohol use
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging and exclusion of other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Chronic epigastric abdominal pain radiating to the back
searchTerms: chronic upper belly pain radiating to back
persistent epigastric pain shooting to back
long-lasting stomach pain with back radiation
poor digestion of fats causing greasy stools
fatty diarrhea due to pancreatic insufficiency
weight loss from poor nutrient absorption

common.symptomName: Diabetes mellitus secondary to endocrine pancreatic insufficiency
searchTerms: high blood sugar due to pancreas failure

common.symptomName: Nausea and vomiting during acute exacerbations
searchTerms: nausea and vomiting during pancreas attacks
jaundice caused by bile duct obstruction
skin and eye yellowing due to blocked bile
weakness due to lack of nutrients
blockages or hardening in pancreas ducts

laboratory: Elevated serum pancreatic enzymes during acute exacerbations
Low fecal elastase indicating exocrine insufficiency
Hyperglycemia consistent with secondary diabetes mellitus
imaging: Pancreatic calcifications on abdominal CT or X-ray
Irregular pancreatic duct with strictures on MRCP or ERCP
Atrophic pancreas with fibrosis on imaging
genetic: No consistent genetic mutations identified in idiopathic late-onset cases
other: Exclusion of alcohol use and other known causes critical for diagnosis

distinguishingFeatures: Similar imaging findings but with clear etiological factor
Characteristic imaging with diffuse pancreatic enlargement

redFlags: Sudden worsening of abdominal pain with signs of acute abdomen
Unexplained weight loss with jaundice suggesting malignancy
Development of diabetes mellitus with rapid progression
references: Yadav D, Lowenfels AB. The epidemiology of pancreatitis and pancreatic cancer. Gastroenterology. 2013 Jun;144(6):1252-61.
Whitcomb DC. Clinical practice. Acute pancreatitis. N Engl J Med. 2006 May 11;354(20):2142-50.
Orphanet: Late-onset idiopathic chronic pancreatitis. ORPHA:700139.
